title: RTPU: Unifying Non-Private and Private Inference with Reconfigurable Architecture
problem: Data centers must simultaneously handle plaintext-based non-private inference and ciphertext-based private inference (via fully homomorphic encryption), but current solutions require costly dedicated accelerators or inflexible general-purpose hardware with poor performance.
motivation: Privacy-preserving inference is increasingly important; unified hardware supporting both plaintext and encrypted computation improves efficiency and reduces deployment costs in heterogeneous data center workloads.
method: RTPU is a reconfigurable multi-core hardware design that performs similar underlying operations for both regular unencrypted tensor math (plaintext) and encrypted homomorphic-encryption math (polynomial ring ciphertext), enabling the same hardware to handle both through fine-grained reconfiguration. It uses kernel group-based scheduling to organize and coordinate computations strategically, optimizing how much of the hardware gets used while maintaining consistent performance (quality of service) for multiple simultaneous jobs with different privacy requirements.
key_novelty: A reconfigurable multi-core architecture that seamlessly switches between regular unencrypted tensor math (plaintext) and encrypted polynomial-ring computations, achieving substantial silicon reuse instead of requiring separate specialized accelerators.
contributions: Unified architecture supporting both non-private and private inference
Substantial silicon reuse between NPI and PI modes
High resource utilization for multi-tenant workloads with kernel group scheduling

metrics.other: High resource utilization for multi-tenant workloads

limitations: No detailed performance numbers provided; comparison with FHE-specific accelerators lacking; scalability to larger homomorphic operations unclear.
primary_theme: Reconfigurable accelerator for private and non-private inference
